title: Rotating habitat, human factors, radiation and life-support audit for OTA-TEC-0082
question: Source-grounded audit of the exact OTA-TEC-0082 CYGNUS CTV dossier. Using primary, peer-reviewed and official human-spaceflight sources, assess only the externally checkable crew-environment layer: (1) verify the rotational-gravity calculation for a 12 m diameter section interpreted as r=6 m and a 0.2 g target, including the resulting angular velocity/rpm; (2) assess evidence on short-radius rotating habitats, Coriolis effects, motion sickness, head-movement sensitivity, adaptation and the limits of extrapolating laboratory/ground studies to a 72-84 h crewed transit; (3) identify what larger-radius/lower-rpm design space would reduce human-factors burden, without changing the fictional CYGNUS geometry automatically; (4) characterize the real cislunar radiation environment for a multi-day crewed transfer, separating GCR background from solar particle events and assessing shielding/storm-shelter implications, including the trade-off created by large windows; (5) assess life-support requirements for a multi-day crewed vehicle, including CO2 removal, humidity/thermal control, water/oxygen consumables or regeneration, fault tolerance and what 'triple redundant life support' would need to mean operationally before it can be treated as an engineering claim; and (6) identify wording that should be narrowed, reclassified or kept [H]/[F/OFFEN]. Do NOT validate or alter fictional crew capacity, fleet availability, introduction dates, operator names, passenger comfort claims, NOXIA costs, unlocks, production values or other gameplay balancing.
why_now: OTA PR #14 explicitly reserved a second source-pinned audit for rotating-habitat human factors, radiation and transfer assumptions after OTA-TEC-0082 entered the canonical OTA->NOXIA pipeline. The production inventory now reports the current CYGNUS blob as uncovered; splitting this crew-environment research from propulsion avoids conflating distinct evidence domains.
real_world_anchor: Rotational artificial-gravity mechanics and human-factors literature; NASA/space-agency cislunar radiation and solar-particle-event guidance; operational environmental-control and life-support evidence from crewed spacecraft and stations.
novelty_reason: First exact-source-revision human-factors, radiation and ECLSS audit for the canonical CYGNUS CTV. Existing OTA technical-object coverage does not test the 6 m-radius/0.2 g habitat or the CYGNUS multi-day crew-environment assumptions.
validation_summary: Der Kandidat ist zum großen Teil bereits eingearbeitet: OTA-TEC-0082-2026-DE fuehrt ihn in der Versionshistorie (v1.2, 2026-08-31) und der Abschluss EXT-KG-OTA-20260831-cygnus-evidence-alignment nennt ihn als Evidenz. Geprueft gegen den Ist-Stand: §5 gibt die Rotationsrechnung korrekt wieder (r = 6 m, 0,2 g -> omega ~ 0,5717 rad/s ~ 5,46 U/min, arithmetisch bestaetigt) und haelt die Tolerabilitaet richtig als [R/H/OFFEN] mit 2 U/min als Designrichtwert statt Komfortgrenze; §9 fuehrt GCR als Hintergrund und SPE als Akutrisiko, Storm-Shelter als realen Ansatz und Fenster ausdruecklich als keinen Null-Schild; §13 kennzeichnet 'dreifach redundante Lebenserhaltung' korrekt als [F]-Label ohne Fehlertoleranzarchitektur; §6 fuehrt den Fenster-Trade-off. Der Life-Support-Teil ist zusaetzlich durch OTA-TEC-0093 abgedeckt (CO2-Entfernung, LiOH vs. regenerativ, Verbrauchsmittel, Redundanzdefinition).
